chunks: Ḥasan ibn ‘Abdillāh ibn Muḥammad ibn ‘Isā narrated to me from his father, from Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb, from someone whose name he mentioned, from ‘Ali ibn ‘Abbās, from Minhāl ibn ‘Amr, and from Asbagh, from Zādhān, who said:
I heard ‘Ali ibn Abī Ťālib (peace be upon him) in al-Raḥbah say: “Ḥasan and Ḥusain are the two flowers (riḥānatā) of the Messenger of Allāh (peace be upon him).”

key_terms.الرَّحْبَة: A specific location in Kufa where Ali (AS) delivered sermons
key_terms.رَسُولِ اللَّهِ: The Messenger of Allah (Prophet Muhammad SAWW)
key_terms.رَيْحَانَتَا: The two flowers or blossoms, indicating endearment and high status

ai.seo_question: What does the term 'Rihnatā' signify regarding Imam Hasan and Imam Husain in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: This narration from Kamil al-Ziyarat records Ali ibn Abi Talib declaring in al-Rahbah that al-Hasan and al-Husayn are the 'riḥānatā' (two blossoms) of the Prophet, a title emphasizing their delicate spiritual status and deep affection. In Shia tradition, this phrase is often linked to the Hadith of al-Kisa, underscoring their unique role as the progeny through whom the Prophet's lineage and imamate continue. The declaration serves as a foundational proof for the love of the Ahl al-Bayt as a means of attaining divine reward.
